question: Which parts of a generated inspection report legitimately differ between two runs of identical code, and are therefore not evidence of anything?
method: DERIVED, NEVER DECLARED. Two LEGACY reports were generated from two separate but identically-parameterised inspections (same site row, same inspection title, same regulatory context, same observation text, same review rationale, same finding conclusion, same corrective action with a literal due date). Whatever differed between them is volatile. A third independent LEGACY run (legacy-C) was then compared against legacy-A using the volatility derived from legacy-A/legacy-B, and came back invariant on all eight cases -- a non-circular control, because legacy-C contributed nothing to the derivation.

volatileFields.position: page 1, line 9 (the cover footer), in every report
volatileFields.origin: shortRef(snapshot.inspection.id) -- the first eight hex characters of the inspection uuid, uppercased
volatileFields.why: Two inspections are two rows. The identifier differs between any two inspections, LEGACY or SHADOW, and naming it is the point of a record reference.

volatileFields.origin: PDFKit stamps wall-clock time at render
volatileFields.why: Two renders a second apart differ. Not content.

volatileFields.origin: PDFKit generates a random file identifier per document
volatileFields.why: Random by construction. Two renders of the SAME snapshot differ here and nowhere else, which is what identified it.

notVolatile: standard text and its 'HazLenz standard summary' label
risk band, severity, likelihood and matrix score
corrective action title, steps, due date, status and priority
byteEqualityVerdict: INAPPROPRIATE between two inspections, and unnecessary. Byte equality IS asserted where it is meaningful: rendering ONE frozen snapshot twice, and rendering it again after poisoning it with governed/shadow fields (test:kg4e-report-field-exclusion), where only /CreationDate, /ModDate and /ID are normalised and every page byte must match.
